correctness.rationale: For all index sets with at least two elements, the intrinsic two-element central-idempotent set consists exactly of the absorbing singleton and E={0} union all diagonal matrix units; E acts on every subset by adding zero. Its image is the characteristic semigroup of subsets containing zero, canonically isomorphic to all binary relations. An independently reconstructed proof of the Magill lemma identifies all its automorphisms using its intrinsic minimal nonzero Green J-class of nonempty rectangles, Green R/L supports, and intersection-incidence rigidity. Any lift with identity restriction fixes each X because EX=X union {0} and the other point of that fiber is already fixed. Index permutations act faithfully. Burnside cycle-index counts yield exactly 2/n! sum 2^c -1, with nonidentity support-k contributions bounded by n^k 2^(-kn/2), proving the asymptotic. Complete tests on n=2,3 verify central idempotents and zero-adjoining identity; independent Burnside and orbit tests verify n<=6.

value.rationale: Complete infinite-family automorphism classification in a structurally distinct noncommutative zero-simple setting. The characteristic zero-containing relation subsemigroup and trivial extension kernel explain precisely why no extra subset-level symmetries survive; this contrasts with natural related power semigroups having enormous hidden fiber permutations. The exact all-element orbit census and factorial-normalized asymptotic measure the quotient complexity of all subsets and are reproducible for every finite n. These are natural structural invariants, not a chosen parameter slice or a minor table correction.
